{"edits": [], "notes": "No edits proposed. The failing test is caused by lines outside the scope of the only finding (app/api_errors.py:10:validator), which is already migrated correctly to @field_validator with @classmethod. The two previously rejected edits were correctly out of scope, so I did not resubmit them.

Root cause of the test failure: error_codes() maps Pydantic errors to codes by matching err["msg"] against v1-style English strings in MESSAGE_CODES ("field required", "value is not a valid integer", "ensure this value has at least"). Pydantic v2 messages differ ("Field required", "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer", "String should have at least 3 characters"). Matching therefore falls through to "INVALID", which is why username and age both return INVALID.

Suggested fix, for a separate finding whose scope covers MESSAGE_CODES and the code lookup: match on the stable error type instead of the message text, which Pydantic v2 provides in err["type"]. For example, MESSAGE_CODES becomes {"missing": "MISSING", "int_parsing": "NOT_AN_INTEGER", "string_too_short": "TOO_SHORT"}, and the lookup becomes code = MESSAGE_CODES.get(err["type"], "INVALID"). Those lines should be re-scoped or given their own finding before they can be edited.

Verified no other v1 APIs remain in this file. Imports (BaseModel, Field, ValidationError, field_validator, Dict, List) are all used, and no Config class or .dict()/.json() calls appear."}
